title: D2
subtitle: Laura in the snow
summary: D2 is Warp's survival horror adventure, first released for Dreamcast in Japan on 23 December 1999.
body: D2 is Warp's survival horror adventure, first released for Dreamcast in Japan on 23 December 1999. Directed by Kenji Eno, it places Laura in the Canadian wilderness after an air disaster, with isolated buildings and creatures interrupting the snow-covered journey. Laura had appeared as the central figure of D, but this game gives her an independent story and a more action-oriented structure. Outdoor exploration uses a third-person view, while interiors shift to first person, changing the player's relationship to the spaces as the journey moves between exposure and shelter.

Monsters interrupt outdoor exploration in random encounters. Laura remains in place during these fights, so the player aims and fires rather than running around the enemy. Victories earn experience and increase her health capacity. A submachine gun supplies unlimited ammunition, while a hunting rifle is used to kill animals for meat that restores health. Hunting therefore connects the landscape to survival between the stranger confrontations. The change between walking, aiming and searching gives the wilderness several purposes, with each interruption asking for a different kind of attention.

Laura also carries a camera, allowing pictures to be taken outside cinematic sequences and saved to a VMU for later viewing. That option creates a quieter activity within an otherwise threatening journey, encouraging the player to stop and look at the surroundings. Eno also composed the music, connecting the game's visual and sonic direction. D2 combines these different tempos within the same isolated setting: an outdoor journey may pause for a photograph or a hunt, then be interrupted by an encounter in which movement gives way entirely to aiming.
